"Sugar Skull Cash" is in the middle of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a smaller share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a reason to be careful.

The table below shows the full count for "Sugar Skull Cash", with every prize level included.
2773.headline: How far along this game is

2774.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "The Price is Right™", about three-quarters are still unsold. The game is still new, with four of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything above about "The Price is Right™" comes from the Texas Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2774.headline: Where this game is in its run

2775.body:
One of Casino 7s's top prizes was claimed in today's numbers. A player in Texas won $100,000. The game started with four top prizes and now has three top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

If you play "Casino 7s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

2780.headline: Early stage or late

2781.body:
"The Perfect Gift" has 503,806 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with 27 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "The Perfect Gift" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2781.headline: What the prize table shows

2782.body:
$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, nearly all is in wins under $10,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2782.headline: What type of game it is

2783.body:
"30X The Cash" has joined the Texas lineup at $2 with five top prizes of $30,000. Only on the first day do the overall odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Today's free summary of "30X The Cash" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2783.headline: A brand-new game to watch

2784.body:
"Lucky Scratch" just went on sale in Texas. The game has eight full prize levels with four top prizes of $100,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

The numbers for "Lucky Scratch" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
